opening.argument: The material presents a conventional museum exhibition, identifying it as “The first-ever exhibition devoted to the portraits of Paul Gauguin.” The National Gallery setting is visibly established through the building and the invitation to “Join us at The National Gallery,” while the exhibition title and booking information are also displayed. The viewer actions described are ordinary attendance steps: “Book tickets online and save,” with members going free. The associated links are framed around exhibition ticketing, social media, or institutional support, rather than a money-making opportunity or a mechanism for transferring personal data. Taken together, the visible artwork, established museum branding, and routine ticketing context support an ordinary cultural and commercial service, without evidence of a deceptive financial or data-collection scheme.
